Three committed scenarios, all green and all RUNNING (no #[ignore], no scheduled-deep-checks exclusion): the named soft-deleted-cohort fold, purge_blocks_by_ids_refuses_a_saturating_subtree_like_the_single_path, and purge_blocks_by_ids_purges_a_live_block_the_single_path_refuses — the former #3819 reproducer, now its regression guard. #3819 was: the op ROOT set filtered to soft-deleted rows while the physical cascade was seeded from the RAW input list, so a LIVE input id was hard-deleted with its whole subtree, emitting no op and no engine fan-out (unsynced local data loss). Fixed by REFUSING a live id (AppError::InvalidOperation, the same refusal purge_block_inner raises) rather than filtering it out of the cascade: filtering would have stopped the loss but left the batch silently skipping what the single path refuses, i.e. permanently divergent from the fold. MISSING ids are still silently dropped by design (nothing to destroy; the chunked empty-trash flow races a concurrent purge) — that asymmetry is deliberate and unoracled
IPC shim over restore_blocks_by_ids_inner

STILL not a clean bill of health, but for a smaller reason than before. Three committed scenarios, all green and all RUNNING (no #[ignore], no scheduled-deep-checks exclusion): the named sibling-cohort fold, restore_blocks_by_ids_omits_the_1884_ancestor_chain_restore (the #3818 reproducer) and restore_blocks_by_ids_skips_a_live_block_the_single_path_refuses (the #3838 reproducer), both now regression guards. #3818 was: the batch cleared deleted_at DOWNWARD only, skipping the #1884 restore_deleted_ancestor_chain the single path runs, so a block restored under a separately-tombstoned parent came back live under an invisible one — absent from the tree render AND from list_trash. Mirroring restore_all_deleted_inner is what hid it: the all-variant restores every tombstone, so the upward walk is vacuous THERE. Fixed by calling the helper once per root (idempotent + op-free, so overlapping chains collapse) and rooting the inheritance recompute at the topmost restored ancestor. #3838 was the mirror image of the #3819 purge asymmetry, left standing one function away: a LIVE input id fell out of the deleted_at IS NOT NULL root filter and was SILENTLY SKIPPED where restore_block_inner REFUSES it, a permanent batch-vs-fold output divergence. Non-destructive (a skipped restore leaves the block tombstoned) but real; fixed the way #3819 was — REFUSE, raising restore_block_inner's "block '<id>' is not deleted" message byte-for-byte rather than filtering — byte-for-byte requires ORDER BY je.key on the probe, since the fold names the first live id in INPUT order while an unordered LIMIT 1 names an index-order one (the same correction was applied to #3819's purge probe, which shipped unordered). MISSING ids are still silently dropped by design, as on the purge path. STILL UNCOVERED, and the only remaining known UNINTENDED gap (the missing-id output divergence — batch Ok(0) vs fold NotFound — is also unpinned, but is deliberate and shared identically with the purge pair): this path skips the in-tx rederive_page_and_space_ids refresh restore_block_inner runs; neither the ancestor-chain nor the live-id fixture can see it (seeded page_id/space_id are already correct on both arms) — catching it needs a scenario that MOVES a block while it is soft-deleted. NOT reachable by this oracle at all: the engine-vs-SQL family #3834 + #3856. #3834 — both paths discarded restore_deleted_ancestor_chain's returned chain and never fanned it out to the engine; batch and fold were EQUALLY wrong, so batch ≡ fold held while the CRDT diverged from SQL on both. #3856 — restore_block_inner does no engine work AT ALL (it never routes through apply_op_projected the way delete_block_inner does), so after #3834 the FOLD converged the restored ancestor while leaving the SEED and its descendant cohort tombstoned in the CRDT, where THIS batch path was already converged — it has hand-rolled dispatch_restore_descendants since #1257. Note what that means for the oracle: #3856 was a genuine batch-vs-fold DIVERGENCE and batch ≡ fold still held, because the arms' op_log and SQL state agreed and only the per-space LoroDoc differed — CRDT state is outside everything this harness snapshots, so widening a scenario would not have found it either. Both are pinned instead by absolute-invariant tests in the same scenario file (restore_block_inner_fans_the_restored_subtree_to_the_engine, its restore_blocks_by_ids_inner sibling, and restore_all_deleted_inner_fans_the_restored_subtree_to_the_engine), which read the engine directly and assert engine/SQL agreement for the ancestor, the seed AND a descendant after a local restore, rather than arm equality

pin: #4259's batch-side live-row fetch, sibling to the five fetch_*_batch kernels and covered by `agaric-engine/tests/reverse_tests.rs::compute_reverse_batch_matches_per_op_loop` — NOT by the `compute_reverse_batch_matches_per_op_fold` proptest the siblings name. That distinction is load-bearing: the proptest only appends to op_log and never inserts `attachments` rows, so every add_attachment in it resolves to None on both kernels, they agree via the row-is-gone fallback, and the entry would stay green with this fetch stubbed to return all-None — the blind-oracle failure this fix exists to close. The _loop test seeds live rows whose fs_path AND filename both differ from the add payload's and pins the absolute value, so a fetch returning the wrong row reddens it. It does NOT cover a duplicate attachment_id within one chunk: its four add_attachment ops carry four distinct ids, and its delete_attachment ops bucket separately. The by-id remap that handles duplicates is therefore unpinned — stated rather than implied, since over-claiming an oracle's reach is the exact failure this entry was corrected for once already.

NOT bulk-named (no batch/bulk/by_ids segment), so the name heuristic cannot see it — but it is the sixth of compute_reverse_batch's hand-copied prior-state kernels, sibling to five *_batch names the heuristic does catch.
